title: 结构体对齐、填充与缓存行占用
expected_output:
=== struct layout, padding and cache lines (line = 64 B) ===

struct A { char a; int b; char c; }
   sizeof=12  align=4  offsetof: a=0 b=4 c=8
   -> 4 bytes of padding: b must sit on a 4-byte boundary

struct B { int b; char a; char c; }
   sizeof= 8  align=4  offsetof: b=0 a=4 c=5
   -> 2 bytes of tail padding only; same fields, 12 -> 8 bytes

struct C { char a; char b; int c; }
   sizeof= 8  align=4  offsetof: a=0 b=1 c=4

sizeof(A) - sizeof(B) = 4 bytes saved just by reordering fields
rule: declare fields from LARGEST to SMALLEST to minimise padding

=== struct P: one cache line per object (false-sharing guard) ===
   sizeof(struct P) = 68 bytes = exactly one 64 B line
   two counters inside struct P occupy DIFFERENT lines -> no false sharing
   two plain ints side by side would share one line -> every write invalidates the peer

=== why this matters ===
   an array of 1e6 struct A objects costs 12 MB; as struct B it costs 8 MB
   fewer bytes touched = fewer cache lines = higher hit rate
